title: Enforce the shared agent-input contract everywhere
decision: The Agent Input Envelope / Prompt Admission Policy applies to every production agent-dispatch path. It is not merely a highest-risk rollout because that could leave forgotten or missed bypass paths.
rationale: Jared explicitly rejected limiting initial application to higher-risk paths: `probably dont just roll it out to higher risk, but everywhere so we dont forget or miss anything.`

title: Design every agent packet for lower-quality capability
decision: Every agent, including agents selected through higher-quality, High-Effort, Overseer, Auditor, verifier, or adjudicator settings, receives the same weak-agent-safe bounded work contract. Puppet Master does not need to identify a model as lower quality before applying the protection.
rationale: User-selected model labels are not dependable capability guarantees; a supposedly higher-quality model may be materially weaker than the product assumes.

title: Use hierarchical reduction for every model role
decision: When source inputs are large, every agent role uses references, bounded slices, and hierarchical reduction rather than receiving a monolithic prompt up to the selected model's context limit.
rationale: The failure mode is not limited to models labeled lower quality, and context-window size does not establish instruction-following reliability.

title: Allow relative model settings to affect routing and execution economics
decision: Model-role settings may change provider/model choice, relative task difficulty, cost, latency, concurrency, and number of bounded passes. They never relax the per-agent objective, acceptance-group, context, evidence, or certification envelope.
rationale: The user may still select a relatively better model for harder work even when both configured models are low quality in absolute terms.

title: Base semantic certification on bounded coverage and evidence
decision: Semantic certification requires a disposition for every requirement ID, evidence references, and an independent bounded verification pass. Missing coverage or unresolved disagreement causes automatic re-splitting/retry or a fail-closed block; a verifier label alone never earns trust.
rationale: Relative model choice can guide role assignment but cannot provide absolute capability assurance.

title: Interpret higher and lower quality as relative within the configured pool
decision: Higher-quality and lower-quality selections remain relative rankings. The relatively higher model is used for harder bounded tasks such as overseeing, reduction, adjudication, or difficult reasoning; the relatively lower model is used for simpler bounded leaf tasks. Both may be low quality in absolute terms and both remain inside the universal safety contract.
rationale: As Jared explained, `the bar for quality is lowered on both`; the ordering remains useful even though neither selection establishes an absolute quality floor.

title: Honor user-selected relative ordering and check hard capabilities separately
decision: The user's model-role selections establish the relative higher/lower ordering used for task-difficulty routing. Puppet Master checks objective hard requirements such as tools, modalities, context support, provider availability, authority, and budget separately; it does not invent an absolute intelligence or semantic-quality score.
rationale: Relative ordering remains meaningful even when both selections are below an assumed industry quality bar, while objective capability mismatches are observable and enforceable.

title: Make lower-model takeover an explicit default-off option
decision: When the relatively higher model is unavailable, Puppet Master does not substitute the relatively lower model into the harder role by default. Safe lower-model takeover may be offered only as an explicit option; its default is no/off. If chosen, universal packet limits, further decomposition, evidence requirements, and bounded verification remain mandatory.
rationale: Jared accepted fallback only conditionally: `Only as an option, but default to no.` Silent fallback could unexpectedly lower effective quality and spend more verification effort.

title: Provide global and one-run lower-model takeover controls
decision: Expose an Advanced global lower-model hard-role fallback setting defaulted off and a receipt-backed one-run recovery action from a blocked run. One-run approval is scoped to that run and does not change the saved global setting.
rationale: This preserves a safe default while allowing explicit recovery when the user accepts additional decomposition, verification, cost, and latency.

title: Require the Agent Input Envelope without predicted budgets
decision: Every dispatch requires a machine-validated Agent Input Envelope with typed identity and lineage, exactly one primary objective, one acceptance group, stable requirement and negative-constraint IDs, bounded source references/windows, allowed tools, output schema, evidence requirements, and stop/escalation conditions. Predicted execution, token, time, retry, cost, and tool-call budgets are not required envelope fields.
rationale: The contract must be machine enforceable, but per-packet budgets would be impossible to predict reliably and would create false precision.

title: Ship one fixed low-end packet profile for strict-policy automated model work
decision: Use one universal Agent Input Envelope profile designed for low-end models across Puppet Master strict-policy automated-system calls. Do not vary it dynamically by model or task, do not make its parameters user adjustable, and do not enlarge it for higher-end automated roles. Users may choose higher-end models and receive better results inside the same strict profile. Direct Assistant Chat and Chat-initiated delegation are separate Chat-controlled lanes and are not forced through this profile.
rationale: This area has already required seven months of work, and dynamic or adjustable automated profiles would materially expand implementation and test scope without being necessary for the low-end-first automation safety goal. Jared later clarified that direct Assistant Chat and the delegation it initiates are controlled by the selected Chat model.

title: Use two fixed measurable split triggers
decision: Beyond exactly one primary objective and one acceptance group, the universal low-end packet profile has only two additional admission triggers: a fixed maximum count of independently auditable mandatory obligation IDs and a fixed maximum fully rendered agent-input size including source text and system-added material. These are shipped constants, not execution forecasts or runtime settings.
rationale: The pair detects both obligation-dense small prompts and text-heavy prompts while avoiding a dynamic multidimensional tuning system.

title: Trigger lossless deterministic splitting when either limit is exceeded
decision: If either fixed split trigger is exceeded, Puppet Master must split the work deterministically, preserve all mandatory requirements, negative constraints, acceptance checks, and source pointers by stable ID, and prove complete assignment through a coverage manifest before dispatch.
rationale: Size enforcement is unsafe if fitting a packet can silently delete or weaken mandatory content.

title: Separate Assistant Chat context management from strict automated packet admission
decision: Direct user-controlled Assistant Chat uses model-aware, continuity-preserving, efficient context assembly for the effective per-thread model, which the user may change mid-thread. It is not forced through the fixed low-end automated Agent Input Envelope. Poor semantic performance from the user's selected Chat model belongs to that user choice. Chat-originated delegation remains under that selected Assistant model's determination; Puppet Master automated systems not initiated by direct Chat remain strict-policy scope.
rationale: Long conversations need context continuity and user model control, while the primary reliability risk being addressed is automated work that Puppet Master itself owns, decomposes, routes, retries, and verifies outside the Chat-origin exception.

title: Use structural and final-rendered admission for strict-policy automated calls
decision: Every strict-policy automated request passes structural Agent Input Envelope admission before assembly and final admission over the fully rendered provider-visible request after all late transforms. A mutation of any bound input invalidates the final rendered admission.
rationale: A structural gate alone cannot detect aggregate size or late obligation injection by instructions, tools, plugins, retrieval, or provider transforms. This is the expert architectural resolution of q-0014; later testing will validate behavior and implementation placement, not whether the second gate exists.

title: Preserve whole-source custody while admitting only bounded semantic views
decision: Controllers and durable stores retain the complete objective and source universe by immutable refs and manifests. Strict-policy automated agents receive only bounded PlanUnit/acceptance/source assignments or deterministic source windows, and synthesis proceeds hierarchically until each request fits the fixed profile.
rationale: Bounded packets must not become lossy source truncation. This resolves q-0015 and is reinforced by Jared's explicit q-0018 yes.

title: Use hash-bound automated admission reuse instead of blind transition rebuilding
decision: Bind each strict-policy automated admission receipt to the rendered request hash, envelope/profile version, route/model/account transform identity, tool-schema set, and source/coverage-manifest hash. Reuse is allowed only for an exact immutable replay under identical bindings; any change requires reassembly and both admission gates.
rationale: This fail-closes changed requests without wasting work on lifecycle events that replay the exact sealed payload. It is the expert refinement of q-0016.

title: Keep Chat-originated delegation under the selected Assistant model's determination
decision: A separate model call does not automatically enter the strict low-end automated packet policy when direct Assistant Chat initiated it. The selected Chat assistant model determines how Chat-originated delegation is shaped and contextualized. Puppet Master automated-system initiation outside that exception remains strict-policy scope.
rationale: Jared explicitly wants the user-selected Chat model, including its quality limitations, to control Assistant Chat behavior rather than applying the automated-system policy merely because the Assistant delegates.

title: Use PlanUnit-first packetization for strict-policy automated Plan work
decision: Strict-policy automated Plan work is assigned by stable PlanUnit IDs plus acceptance/source refs. Generated shards are navigation and lineage projections rather than assumed-safe packet boundaries. Any PlanUnit group or individual PlanUnit that exceeds the fixed profile is split further with stable lineage and lossless coverage.
rationale: Jared answered yes, and live repository inspection confirms that generated shards can still be tens of thousands of lines.

title: Defer feature and model testing until the explicit testing phase
decision: Complete the remaining product and architecture conversation before discussing or running the behavioral/model testing program. No low-end model experiments, threshold trials, reduction-fidelity tests, retry tests, or automation-surface tests are authorized in the current phase. Structural validation of the planning ledger remains allowed.
rationale: Jared explicitly said the system needs testing but does not want testing now and wants to discuss the rest of the design first.

title: Centralize strict-policy automated packet compilation and admission
decision: One shared backend Agent Packet Compiler and Admission Gate owns strict-policy work-intent intake, packet construction and splitting, provider-visible rendering, both admission gates, coverage manifests, and admission receipts. Feature systems may not independently assemble bypass provider prompts.
rationale: Jared answered `I think yes`; architectural centralization prevents per-feature drift. His uncertainty is preserved as a later weak-model testing obligation rather than an open architecture question.

title: Use typed controller-admitted follow-ups for missing automated context
decision: A strict-policy automated agent that lacks context returns a typed request naming the exact missing requirement IDs, PlanUnits, source refs/windows, or evidence category and rationale. The controller supplies only the smallest sufficient context through a newly admitted follow-up packet with preserved lineage; unbounded self-expansion is prohibited.
rationale: Jared answered `I think yes`. The protocol is the safe architectural default; whether low-quality agents reliably request useful context remains a deferred testing question.

title: Use bounded typed hierarchical reduction with fail-closed completion
decision: Split-work results merge only through bounded hierarchical reducers consuming typed per-requirement dispositions, evidence refs, uncertainty, missing-context states, and disagreements. Final completion requires complete obligation coverage and disposition of contradictions; raw child transcripts are never concatenated into one final prompt.
rationale: Jared answered `I think yes`. This prevents the merge stage from recreating the original large-prompt failure; weak-model reduction fidelity remains explicitly untested until the later phase.

title: Build unstructured-source obligation inventories through bounded redundant extraction
decision: Before strict-policy execution packetization, deterministically segment unstructured source into immutable overlapping windows, assign every span to bounded independent extraction, prove source-span coverage, and reconcile source-linked obligation manifests hierarchically. Exact fixed overlap and redundancy constants remain for the deferred testing phase.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. This prevents the obligation-identification stage from sending the same original large source to one model and recreating the failure before packetization begins.

title: Preserve exact source spans and unresolved obligation classification
decision: Every extracted obligation retains its exact immutable source span and typed classification. Unresolved material remains in the mandatory reconciliation set and cannot be silently downgraded to context or omitted from execution coverage.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Exact source lineage makes weak-extractor errors inspectable and prevents uncertain classification from acting as deletion.

title: Fail closed on unresolved obligation meaning or conflicts
decision: Unresolved mandatory meaning or contradictory obligations block strict-policy execution. The bounded dispute escalates first to the relatively higher configured oversight model; if unresolved, it remains blocked or seeks user adjudication when available. The relatively lower model cannot assume the hard adjudication role unless the existing explicit default-off override is chosen.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Proceeding under unresolved meaning would turn uncertainty into silent omission or invented compromise.

title: Enforce strict-policy admission at the provider-dispatch boundary
decision: Every strict-policy automated provider dispatch requires a valid shared-compiler admission receipt bound to the effective rendered request and routing identities. Missing, stale, mismatched, or invalid receipts are rejected. Legacy and feature-local raw-prompt paths are blocked migration defects rather than compatibility fallbacks.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Shared compiler ownership is only machine-enforced when the final dispatch boundary cannot bypass it.

title: Persist compact content-addressed receipt chains without sensitive duplication
decision: Strict-policy runs retain linked content-addressed census, coverage, packet, admission, context-expansion, reduction, disagreement, and final-coverage receipts. Receipts use stable IDs, hashes, versions, dispositions, and governed refs without duplicating full prompts, source bodies, secrets, or sensitive tool results; existing custody and retention owners remain authoritative.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. This preserves auditability, replay safety, and invalidation evidence without creating another uncontrolled large-context or secret store.

title: Expose concise packet status and advanced diagnostics without tuning controls
decision: Normal run surfaces show concise preparation, split, context-request, retry, and blocked states with stable receipt IDs where useful. Detailed manifests remain available through advanced diagnostics subject to permissions and redaction. Packet-size, obligation-count, overlap, redundancy, and model-specific tuning controls are not user-adjustable.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. This balances actionable transparency with the fixed low-end profile and avoids turning implementation constants into unsupported user knobs.

title: Derive provider enforcement from trusted controller-issued execution origin
decision: Every provider-bound request carries a non-self-asserted controller-issued `execution_origin`. Provider admission derives strict-policy versus accepted Chat-lane handling from that trusted value. Unknown origin fails closed, automated callers cannot declare themselves Chat traffic, and model identity or mid-thread model changes do not determine execution origin.
rationale: Jared answered yes. Without trusted provenance, the accepted direct-Chat exception would become a bypass label for automated or legacy calls.

title: Require a closed-world registry for every production provider-dispatch route
decision: Every production provider route has a stable route ID, owner, allowed execution origins, enforcement mode, and migration status. Unknown or unmigrated automated routes are blocked. Direct Assistant Chat and Chat-initiated delegation exceptions are explicitly enumerated, never wildcarded or self-asserted.
rationale: Jared answered yes. The registry supplies completeness evidence that individual provider-gate failures cannot provide and keeps planned-route inventory distinct from implemented migration status.

title: Fail closed and resume from verified receipts when packet enforcement infrastructure fails
decision: Unavailable or corrupt strict-policy compiler, admission, or receipt infrastructure produces a typed durable blocked state, never a raw-prompt fallback. Recovery resumes from the latest verified immutable receipt, and any changed effective content or routing binding causes reconstruction from the earliest affected stage and fresh admission.
rationale: Jared answered yes. This preserves both work and enforcement under availability pressure without treating bypass as recovery.

title: Reconstruct every strict-policy automated turn from bounded typed current state
decision: Strict-policy automation does not accumulate append-only model conversation history. Each provider turn is rebuilt from the current bounded assignment, typed state, required decisions, evidence refs, and independently admitted exact excerpts; prior transcripts remain in durable custody. Direct Assistant Chat remains in its separate user-controlled context lane.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Bounded initial prompts do not prevent retries, tool loops, or long-lived automation from growing later turns unless every turn is reconstructed and re-admitted.

title: Route every model-visible tool and data result through bounded evidence admission
decision: All tool, MCP, plugin, terminal, search, file, vision, memory, and other result content shown to a strict-policy automated model passes through a shared bounded evidence adapter. Oversized raw output remains under governed custody while exact refs, source-linked slices, or typed summaries are admitted into a final-rendered provider request.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Raw tool output is a major later-turn context-growth path and must not bypass packet limits, permissions, or source lineage.

title: Validate and boundedly repair agent responses before reduction
decision: Every strict-policy agent response passes schema, assigned-obligation-ID, evidence-reference, uncertainty, and coverage validation before reducer or completion admission. Malformed or incomplete responses receive a bounded defect-only protocol-repair packet. Exhausting the fixed policy-owned attempt limit escalates or blocks; invalid output is never merged, and the exact limit is deferred to testing.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Hardening input alone cannot prevent silent omissions if downstream systems accept unusable, partial, or contract-breaking agent responses.

title: Isolate untrusted evidence from instruction authority
decision: Every strict-policy packet carries a typed instruction-authority manifest. Source, retrieval, memory, and tool content remain untrusted evidence and cannot alter the controller objective, response contract, tool permissions, write scope, or override authority. Prompt Pipeline and policy owners define the authority contract; FileSafe independently consumes and checks the final compiled request. Unresolved authority conflicts fail closed, and a parser or detector miss never authorizes execution.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation and flagged FileSafe ties. Six bounded gpt-5.6-sol medium reads of live FileSafe canon confirm this owner split: FileSafe is a mandatory downstream safety enforcer, not the semantic prompt or instruction-authority owner.

title: Use content-addressed dependency invalidation with owner-bounded FileSafe currentness
decision: Census, packet, admission, response, reduction, completion, and guard receipts participate in a content-addressed dependency-version graph. Changed dependencies stale only affected descendants and force minimal rebuild before downstream use. Prompt Pipeline and work-packet owners control semantic branch invalidation; FileSafe supplies an independently current guard node and final mutation CAS rather than owning conversation or packet invalidation.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. The FileSafe audit found strong hash, identity, stale-input, and filesystem-CAS precedents but no general PlanUnit/policy/schema/skill/transform/route dependency graph, confirming the need for this cross-owner contract.

title: Provide bounded source-linked human adjudication without weakening FileSafe
decision: Unresolved semantic conflicts reach the user through a bounded source-linked decision surface with exact disputed spans, interpretations, affected requirement IDs, consequences, and correction. The outcome becomes a typed decision receipt. Decision Policy and Contracts own authority, GUI owners project it, and storage/event owners persist it. A semantic decision receipt never grants FileSafe permission or override authority; security reductions require separate authenticated scoped receipts.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation and requested FileSafe review. FileSafe canon supplies persistent blocked outcomes, ordered owner-issued actions, authenticated override constraints, and visible reasons, but not the general semantic adjudication contract; the boundaries must remain explicit.

title: Require co-bound independent Agent Admission and FileSafe gates
decision: Every strict-policy automated provider dispatch requires both an Agent Admission receipt and a FileSafe guard receipt over the same final effective provider payload, structured attachments, and route binding. Agent Admission proves fixed-profile obligation coverage; FileSafe proves safety and authorization. Neither substitutes for the other, and any post-gate mutation invalidates both before dispatch.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Separate proofs over different payloads would leave a late-transform gap, while combining the authorities would make semantic coverage or security enforcement weaker and harder to audit.

title: Keep semantic adjudication incapable of granting FileSafe authority
decision: A semantic human-adjudication receipt cannot authorize a FileSafe-blocked command, file access, mutation, or enforcement reduction. FileSafe recovery exposes only canonical ordered owner-issued `allowed_action_ids`, `preserved_local_work`, prerequisites, reason codes, and bounded detail refs. Any permitted weakening requires a distinct authenticated, scoped, expiring, auditable FileSafe override receipt; GUI projections cannot mint, reorder, or broaden actions.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Resolving ambiguous requirements and granting sensitive or destructive authority are different acts and must remain separately authenticated, scoped, persisted, and audited.

title: Bind FileSafe guard receipts to exact safety-relevant currentness
decision: Every FileSafe guard receipt binds the compiled payload and structured-attachment digests and provenance, instruction bundle and runtime binding, run/node/attempt and provider-route identity, permission snapshot, canonical root, read/write scope, allowlist and security-baseline versions, relevant override receipt, and mutation-target read revision where applicable. Any changed, missing, ambiguous, or stale bound input forces FileSafe re-check before dispatch, tool invocation, file access, promotion, or mutation.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. A general packet dependency graph cannot safely reuse a FileSafe decision unless FileSafe's concrete safety-currentness vector remains exact and independently valid.

title: Compile least-authority instruction and capability bundles
decision: Every strict-policy packet activates only mandatory-global safety and runtime instructions and objective-required tools, skills, personas, plugin contributions, schemas, and policy fragments. Each active component carries stable identity, version, authority class, and inclusion reason; unrelated catalogs are omitted or referenced, all included material counts toward the fixed rendered-input ceiling, and no new adjustable profile or threshold is introduced.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Weak agents can be overloaded by irrelevant instruction branches and capability catalogs even when a packet fits its fixed size and obligation limits.

title: Send only an immutable co-gated provider dispatch intent
decision: After the deterministic Packet Admission Gate and FileSafe program approve one final request, the provider adapter sends only an immutable dispatch-intent snapshot binding exact provider bytes, the structured-attachment manifest, both receipt identities, route/model/account and transform identity, and run/node/attempt identity. Reconstruction or any changed binding creates a new intent and requires both program gates again; exact retries retain one immutable identity.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. An immutable intent closes the time-of-check/time-of-use gap between program validation and provider transmission without adding another model call.

title: Keep reusable derivations distinct from execution authority
decision: Dependency-current source windows, obligation censuses, normalized evidence, and reductions may be reused across runs as derived data with exact provenance. Packet Admission Gate, FileSafe, operator-override, and dispatch-intent receipts remain non-transferable execution authority bound to their exact run/node/attempt, route, permission, and currentness context; each new run obtains fresh program-gate authority before dispatch or mutation.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation. Reuse should reduce repeated source-processing and model usage without allowing cached artifacts or prior-run security decisions to authorize new execution.

title: Use deterministic program gates with zero hidden per-dispatch model calls
decision: The ordinary strict-policy path is deterministic packet compilation, deterministic Packet Admission Gate validation, deterministic FileSafe enforcement, one assigned worker-model call, and deterministic response-conformance validation. Infrastructure gates add zero mandatory model calls per ordinary dispatch. Model-based obligation extraction is limited to upstream processing of new or changed unstructured sources without an authoritative census and is reused while dependency-current. Explicit workflow worker, reviewer, verifier, Overseer, extraction, and repair calls remain visible model work roles rather than hidden gates.
rationale: Jared accepted the recommendation after explicitly raising concern about too much agent usage. Program gates can prove machine-verifiable structure, coverage, currentness, permissions, and schemas without introducing two extra prompt-reading models or falsely claiming semantic understanding.

title: Run cross-system tests locally with exactly eight low-end and two high-end models
decision: Open the empirical testing phase across essentially every affected automated model-call surface except direct Assistant Chat and Chat-originated delegation. Local GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra task `019fc3fd-4061-7d01-9c22-a3c82f34de1f` owns the closed-world impact inventory, test design, preregistration, pilot, exactly eight low-end and two high-end subject-model runs, evidence, and terminal results against the exact dirty checkout. Every test write is confined to `/Users/jaredsmacbookair/Documents/PuppetMaster/tests/agent_packet_restrictions/`; every other repo path is read-only to it. The active ledger task performs no feature/model testing. The testing task distinguishes currently executable tests, isolated contract simulations, and production-integration tests blocked until implementation exists.
rationale: Jared corrected that a worktree cannot represent the large uncommitted and unpushed branch state, required tests to live and operate in one specific folder, and fixed the subject matrix at exactly eight low-end models and two high-end models.

title: Treat the August 5 packet as an additive noncanonical course-correction source
decision: Ingest the supplied prompt-complexity automation handoff as source-lineage and design input without restarting the existing project, discarding current atoms or test artifacts, editing canonical Plans, resuming testing, or treating the packet's internal decision labels as canonical product authority. Preserve its ZIP path and SHA-256, exact central rule and negative constraints, source-map noncanonical boundary, and validation-receipt discrepancies. Reconcile its content against live Plans and the active ledger before any future compile.
rationale: The packet explicitly says it is additive and not a substitute for canonical Plans. Live inspection found useful coherent content but stale validation metadata, so its substantive delta can inform planning while its receipt and schema names cannot authorize execution or canonical promotion.

title: Add Context Admission and PromptCapsule upstream without weakening the final gate pair
decision: Use a distinct deterministic Context Admission Gate and external Context Receipt to select and account for phase-relevant material before PromptCapsule compilation. Then render the provider request and retain the existing independent deterministic Packet Admission Gate and FileSafe checks over the same final effective bytes, followed by immutable dispatch intent and deterministic response conformance. Context admission proves neither obligation completeness of final rendered bytes nor safety authority and cannot substitute for either final gate.
rationale: This preserves the packet's central context-selection correction while protecting the already accepted separation among obligation admission, FileSafe safety, immutable dispatch, and zero hidden gate-model calls.

title: Externalize deterministic obligations and compile a least-authority context bundle
decision: Retain complete reference contracts and durable state in governed stores, but compile each automated turn from stable obligation IDs and owner dispositions into one bounded PromptCapsule containing only task-required behavior, rules, sources, selected skills/tools/MCP schemas, effective access, acceptance, and output contract. Persona remains behavior-only and cannot grant permission or route authority. Detailed history, artifacts, policies, catalogs, and operational state are tool-fetched or artifact-backed; validators and runtime services enforce deterministic rules instead of repeating their algorithms as prose.
rationale: The live ledger already requires bounded least-authority packets and deterministic gates. The handoff extends that design with explicit ownership categories and Persona/rule/tool compilation without deleting obligations.

title: Separate specialist coverage, sustainable concurrency, and relative model-role routing
decision: Preserve every required independent specialist result while allowing the Orchestrator to execute sustainable provider/resource-aware waves and reserve capacity for parent synthesis, testing, verification, and repair. Temporary scarcity produces durable queue/checkpoint/wait state rather than erased work or false completion. User-facing planning, architecture, research judgment, cross-owner adjudication, and synthesis use the relatively higher configured role; lower configured roles receive bounded test-proven units and no final authority. The higher/lower ordering remains relative and lower-role takeover remains explicit and default-off.
rationale: The packet correctly distinguishes coverage from simultaneous fanout and harder from bounded leaf work. The wording is normalized to Jared's accepted relative-role model instead of assuming absolute model quality.

title: Preserve the preflight evidence and redesign only the future post-V4 method
decision: Keep the existing 54-surface inventory, 24 implementation-gated tests, 7 semantic cases, 222 deterministic checks, zero-call counts, V1-V3 failures, V4 invalidation, and exact hashes as preregistration/control-plane history. Do not relabel them as empirical results or rerun unaffected work automatically. A future explicitly authorized post-V4 method may add matched legacy-full-prompt versus compiled-capsule/runtime-service variants and before/after token and InstructionLoad measurements, but it must freeze a corrected method, exact route roster, compiler/runtime/scorer/capture versions, acceptance margins, and ten route canaries before semantic pilot. q-0022 remains deferred and candidate atom-0062 grants no testing authority.
rationale: The handoff says preserve evidence and compare native capsules rather than restart. The terminal closeout proves no subject baseline exists, so preservation means keeping drafts and failures, not pretending testing already happened.

title: Adjudicate the August 8 final packet as noncanonical source input, not an execution prompt
decision: Accept `PM_Prompt_Complexity_Final_Course_Correction_2026-08-08.zip` as a noncanonical course-correction source after validating its archive and manifest. Do not automatically execute its implementation or audit prompts, edit canonical Plans, run tests, or create a testing task. Preserve the packet SHA-256 `7e2c87155b781fdefdcc3c83e5120aeac51b157aea5a4133f10379f59951dc29`, all reviewed requirements, and its precedence defect: `REFERENCE_SUPERSESSIONS.md` names `PROVIDER_CLI_FINAL_ADJUDICATION.md` as highest provider authority although that file is absent from the archive and manifest. Therefore provider-policy claims remain proposals requiring live canonical reconciliation.
rationale: Jared explicitly gave this task authority to decide which embedded prompts should be followed. The architecture content is useful, while the missing highest-precedence provider file prevents the packet from self-proving a complete provider adjudication and no current request authorizes implementation or audit execution.

title: Resolve profile calibration as one fixed contract plus diagnostic InstructionLoad
decision: Keep one universal conservative structural and safety contract designed for the weakest supported automated role, with no predicted per-task budgets and no dynamic, user-adjustable, task-specific, tier-specific, or model-specific strict profiles. Measure actual section tokens, InstructionLoad, adapter/route facts, and outcomes; use them for deterministic splitting, retrieval, queueing, escalation, and future evidence review. Relative configured roles may receive different bounded task difficulty, but stronger routes do not receive larger unstructured obligation packets or wider authority.
rationale: This preserves Jared's exact one-size/no-budget decisions while incorporating the final packet's useful distinction between durable state, admitted context, actual instruction load, provider adapter facts, and observed model behavior.

title: Adopt typed stages, stable rendering, transactional compaction, conditional rules, recovery, and compact resource projection
decision: Extend the accepted Context Admission and PromptCapsule architecture with: stable versioned prefixes and exact cache/dependency invalidation; typed Goal and Planning stage transitions; semantically coherent stable-ID slices; transactional artifact-backed compaction; deterministic conditional instruction deltas; typed progressive tool/MCP/skill recovery with renewed admission; and compact server/provider/resource projections with ObservableWork. All mechanisms preserve exact lineage, one bounded objective, independent final Packet Admission and FileSafe checks, immutable final provider bytes, resumability, and honest completion. No Playwright-shaped production runtime or new SQLite store is introduced.
rationale: These mechanisms move deterministic complexity out of giant prose prompts while preserving the safety, lineage, validation, specialist, and completion obligations that cannot be deleted.

title: Keep BSD outside the mandatory path and default it Off
decision: Treat BSD as a possible separate bounded advisor-model call, not a deterministic gate or mandatory prompt reader. Default it Off until dedicated testing qualifies its intervention value, false-positive and false-negative behavior, usage, latency, and failure semantics. Any later Auto or On mode requires explicit policy, visible usage attribution, reserved capacity, typed immutable inputs and outputs, no authority widening, and normal deterministic admission of any proposed delta.
rationale: The packet's Auto default would add recurring agent usage before evidence exists and conflicts with Jared's concern about multiple models rereading each prompt. The ordinary deterministic path is complete without BSD.

title: Retire the old testing task and hold successor subject testing for Jared's new plan
decision: Do not resume task `019fc3fd-4061-7d01-9c22-a3c82f34de1f`; preserve it as terminal historical preflight evidence. Supersede the exact 8-low/2-high cohort, A-E proposal, and old post-V4 resume recipe. Prefer a fresh GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra successor after canonical architecture reconciliation and a refreshed affected-surface census. Prepare that successor only through a bounded deterministic zero-provider-call preflight. When it is ready to test with subject agents, notify Jared and stop for his exact model roster and testing-method plan. No test-task creation, route canary, pilot, fleet, provider, or subject-model call is authorized now.
rationale: The old task ran no subject tests and its method was invalidated before freeze, while the product architecture has materially changed. Starting clean at the testing-control-plane boundary avoids inheriting obsolete assumptions without discarding valid artifacts or failures.

title: Keep Assistant Chat and concept visuals externally owned while specifying shared runtime truth
decision: Preserve direct Assistant Chat as a separate thread-local, user-model-controlled context lane. This architecture may define typed Context Lens, compaction, branching, command, Goal visibility, attachment, provider/cache warning, BSD usage, and ObservableWork contracts consumed by user-facing surfaces, but it does not redesign or edit Settings, Assistant Chat, PMConcept7, Usage, or Planning visual concepts. GUI controls display or request backend state; they do not grant authority or bypass deterministic gates.
rationale: The final packet properly identifies shared runtime inputs, while Jared's earlier correction requires Chat to be approached differently and the handoff explicitly protects other concept owners from edits in this lane.

title: Route successor preparation through Sol max, medium, and xhigh by task difficulty
decision: Run the new prompt-complexity successor with GPT-5.6 Sol max as the main controller. Use GPT-5.6 Sol medium subagents for easier bounded mechanical or deterministic preparation and GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh subagents for harder bounded architecture, scoring, test-design, adjudication, or synthesis preparation. title: Resolve the subject roster and frozen-snapshot first-attempt method
decision: Answer q-0022 with the tested roster GPT-5.4 mini xhigh, GPT-5.4 mini medium, and GPT-5.6 Luna medium. Use a current unfinished Plans snapshot copied into the exclusive disposable test root; bind every revision, capsule, oracle, scorer, reducer, and result to exact hashes; preserve every first attempt; prohibit retry, best-of, and replacement within a revision; reuse passes only by exact hash; and rerun only transitively invalidated paths after a general architecture change. rationale: Jared supplied the roster and corrected the method after deterministic preflight. The frozen snapshot prevented unrelated live Plans drift from terminating disposable testing, while first-attempt preservation kept all failures and invalid cells visible.

title: Assign mechanical fields to deterministic owners and semantic judgments to models
decision: Compile automated work so models own only bounded semantic judgments. Candidate eligibility, stale-authority resolution, direct facts and exact types, joins and ordering, taxonomy canonicalization, patch paths and encoding, byte/hash accounting, bindings, finding closure, unsupported-target absence, and terminal projection are deterministic program responsibilities. Stage-specific conformance rejects malformed semantic output before deterministic projection.
rationale: Across R5 and R6, weak and stronger tested routes repeatedly reached the intended meaning but failed filtering, copied facts, type encoding, JSON Pointer/Patch formatting, or cryptographic closure. Moving those nonsemantic obligations to generic deterministic owners enabled all three paths to complete without replacing prior failures.

title: Use admitted per-candidate and per-comparison semantic micro-units
decision: Deterministically remove unsupported or already-resolved candidates before provider rendering. Give a weak model one typed candidate, comparison, audit decision, cross-topic edge, or one-role/one-new-edge semantic objective with the exact endpoint decisions and cited records needed for that objective. Join, order, reduce, and assemble outputs deterministically using stable IDs and exact lineage. Split any grouped or mixed-objective packet when those semantics can be isolated.
rationale: Both medium routes selected unsupported B-T03 from a 74,503-byte R5 packet; later grouped edge and broad-audit units failed when relevant alignment or comparison records were absent. R6's admitted micro-units plus deterministic reducers preserved meaning and completed all three configured paths.

title: Persist disposable test Goals through recoverable failures
decision: Define a disposable test Goal around the full empirical objective rather than one audit or repair attempt. Preserve ordinary harness, prompt, oracle, scorer, controller, and subject failures; repair the test lane or mint a new general revision; and continue until the configured matrix reaches an honest durable terminal. Stop only for a genuinely external impasse outside the authorized test root. This rule does not authorize hidden production retries or broaden canonical, provider, permission, or implementation scope.
rationale: Repeated artificial one-attempt terminals prevented any subject execution. Jared explicitly corrected that behavior, and the persistent R5-to-R6 sequence produced useful failure evidence and ultimately a valid matrix without rewriting first attempts.

title: Accept R6 as scoped evidence and hold canonical compile for explicit instruction
decision: Accept `VALID_COMPLETED_FROZEN_SNAPSHOT_MATRIX` as evidence that the cumulative semantic/decomposition architecture completed for all three configured paths on the exact frozen fifteen-file fixture. Preserve 104 first-attempt calls as 83 PASS, 15 FAIL, and 6 INVALID/no-credit with zero retries, best-of, or replacements. Treat the result as satisfying the testing-before-compile prerequisite for ledger review only. It does not prove current Plans, full Planning Wizard behavior, production enforcement, release readiness, safety, general weak-model safety, or grant automatic compile authority. Canonical Plans remain unchanged until Jared explicitly requests compile.
rationale: The terminal is an honest successful causal simulation with strong failure preservation and counterfactual protection, but its own evidence boundary excludes production and canonical claims. The correct next phase is user review and an explicit compile decision, not automatic promotion.

title: Run one unchanged fresh R6-v7 repeatability replicate across all three configured paths
decision: Authorize successor task `019ffbff-994a-76f0-9c06-57bab28b7ee3` to create a new non-budgeted Goal and execute `PW-R7-REPLICATION-20260814.1` on pm-dev under `/mnt/Cursor/PuppetMaster`. Only a separately preregistered replicate with fresh independent model calls and an unchanged protocol can answer that question without selection bias. Guaranteeing a pass through retries or tuning would defeat the requested verification.

title: Iterate generic fixes until one frozen candidate passes two complete fresh matrices consecutively
decision: After the existing R7 Goal closes with its preserved honest terminal, authorize successor task `019ffbff-994a-76f0-9c06-57bab28b7ee3` to create a new non-budgeted Goal for `PW-R8-ITERATIVE-FIX-TWO-CLEAN-RUNS-20260815`. It must diagnose semantic and controller failures, create explicit generic candidate revisions under the exclusive test root, use counterfactual holdouts, freeze before every run, and continue automatically through failed runs and evidence-driven repairs. A run may count only when all three configured model paths and every required semantic and deterministic stage complete with fresh newly created test-taker tasks, zero subject failures, invalid or missing cells, retries, best-of, replacements, or hidden repairs, and validated durable terminals. The Goal completes only after two consecutive counted passes on byte-identical final architecture, prompts, contracts, scorers, oracles, reducers, fixture, phase order, routes, and acceptance rules. Any failure, invalid/incomplete run, unproven identity, or architecture/protocol change resets the streak to zero. Preserve every attempt and do not edit canonical Plans, the ledger, Concepts, governance, or production implementation.
rationale: A single successful run did not reproduce reliably. Iterative repair is appropriate, but qualification must distinguish development from evidence: failures guide a new frozen candidate, while two independent unchanged all-pass matrices with fresh subjects provide a materially stronger repeatability signal without retry selection or between-run tuning.

title: Qualify only end-to-end native Goal Mode prompt execution at both controller and subject layers
decision: The prompt architecture and its empirical qualification must use actual Puppet Master Goal Mode at both layers. The design/test controller owns one durable parent Goal/GoalRun. Each autonomous prompt or test-taker case is a fresh Goal-owned execution, normally a child Goal linked to that parent, with admitted identity/policy/route/context, durable state and continuation, typed evidence, child settlement, verification, and completion receipt. Multiple low-level model/provider/tool turns inside one bounded Goal do not each mint a new Goal. Any standalone non-Goal prompt result has zero final qualification credit even if its semantic answer passes. Preserve such results as lower-level evidence. Freeze canary and matrix credit until the test harness exercises the actual Goal Runtime lifecycle. Direct Assistant Chat remains separately governed.
rationale: Jared reports that Goal Mode was the only mechanism that allowed models to pass the Plans audit process; the missing Goal lifecycle is therefore part of the causal architecture, not incidental transport. Canonical Goal Runtime independently supports one persistent workflow Goal, first-class child Goals for autonomous bounded work, multiple runtime turns within each Goal, parent-owned synthesis/certification, and typed completion receipts.

title: Make Goal Mode local and mandatory for every fresh test taker
decision: For every independently scored subject invocation, create a new test-taker task or agent and require that test taker itself to activate actual Goal Mode before the subject prompt is admitted. Either Codex native Goal Mode or Oh My Pi native Goal Mode may be used in this disposable test lane. Record and bind the test-taker identity, Goal creation/activation receipt, objective and criteria, model/route/control state, subject-input identity, all in-Goal turns, and terminal Goal state/receipt. Fail closed with zero empirical credit if any of those bindings are missing. A controller parent Goal or child-goal relationship remains necessary orchestration context but is not sufficient test-taker proof. Each test-taker task, Goal, conversation, and continuation state is single-use. Preserve prior plain-prompt evidence as diagnostics only and keep the two-clean qualification streak at zero until the corrected harness is frozen.
rationale: Jared explicitly corrected the earlier hierarchy wording: every fresh test taker—not merely the controller workflow or a logically Goal-owned child—must use Goal Mode. Allowing Codex or OMP native Goal Mode lets the disposable harness test the causal execution property now without confusing either transport with eventual canonical Puppet Master production authority.

title: Keep the existing external OMP lane on the Windows P-drive launch boundary
decision: Treat the already arranged external Oh My Pi lane as a Windows-hosted process launched with exact command form `omp --cwd P:\`. Bind its durable sandbox custody to `/mnt/Cursor/OMP-Sandboxes/pm-prompt-controller-ox-alpha-20260821` on the NAS-facing filesystem. Do not use Linux `ps` as OMP liveness evidence and do not launch a duplicate Linux-side process. Retain the per-test-taker Goal Mode requirement: after OMP launch, each fresh independently scored OMP test taker must activate OMP native Goal Mode before subject work.
rationale: Jared supplied the exact host and invocation. Preserving the Windows-versus-NAS path mapping avoids false stopped-process diagnoses and duplicate agents while keeping process transport distinct from Goal Mode activation evidence.

title: Use native OMP slash-command activation rather than prompt-instructed Goal simulation
decision: For OMP-based controller and test-taker qualification, launch a saved interactive session and enter native Goal Mode through the TUI `/goal <objective>` command before any model task turn. Require durable `mode_change:goal`, `goal-mode-context`, Goal ID/objective binding, model identity, and hidden `goal` tool evidence; require terminal Goal evidence for every completed scored invocation. Treat positional CLI prompts and prompts that merely instruct the model to create or pretend to use a Goal as non-Goal executions with zero qualification credit. Keep OMP advisor disabled and preserve the exact Windows `P:\` launch and independent sandbox boundary.
rationale: The failed restart demonstrated that a regular initial prompt leaves Goal Mode inactive, while OMP's native interactive command creates the persistent Goal and exposes the hidden tool before model work. This deterministic client-side activation is the only defensible way to test Jared's requirement that the controller and every fresh test taker actually use Goal Mode.
